en: Now, for the sake of accomplishing the mudrās, their characteristics are stated here;
by knowing which, one obtains the fruit of the ritual application of all mantras. (1)
Śodhanī, Kālakarṇī, Mukulī, Śaśakarṇikā, Niṣṭhurā, Padmamudrā, Namaskārā, and Manoramā. || 2 ||
Śāntā, Liṅgamudrā, Dhvajā, and likewise Āvāhanī;
Gāyatrī and the Netramantra are thus proclaimed. || 3 ||
Having joined the bases of the hands together and likewise the regions of the hearts, one should then strike the palms; this mudrā is known as the Purifying (Śodhanī). || 4 ||
Then, having formed fists with the fingers extended upward and the thumbs joined at their tips, one should display the *kālakarṇī* mudrā to the people.
Having joined the two hands together, one should display a hollow space between them,
forming a closed fist in the shape of a lotus bud.
Having bent the two index fingers, one should place them at the tips of those [two hands];
the heads of the two thumbs should be joined, while the remaining fingers are straight, firm, and even.
Having placed [the hand] at the wrist of the left, one should likewise place the right;
this mudrā is to be known as Śaśakarṇī in the practice of yoga. 8.
Having formed the añjali with both hands, the wise one should form two fists;
having placed the two thumbs inside [the fists], he should employ the Niṣṭhurā mudrā. 9.
The previously mentioned *mukuli* [mudrā], with the fingers extended toward the region of the heart, should display the *padmamudrā*, which has the form of a blossoming lotus. 10.
With both hands joined at all the fingers and placed against the region of the heart,
she is to be saluted by all, while pressing down with the left thumb.
When the hands are to be folded, the little fingers should be turned upward;
of those two, the left one is to be known as being on the outside, or alternatively, when the middle fingers are also folded.
Having bent the tips of the ring fingers and joined them with the palms of one's own hands, one should extend the two index fingers and join their tips together. 13.
The two thumbs are placed at the base joints of those very [fingers] and are bent;
this is renowned as Manoramā, which bestows union with Śiva. 14.
With the tips of the index finger and thumb joined, and the remaining fingers straight, dense, and even—this is proclaimed as the "Peaceful" mudrā for all mantras. 15.
Having formed the *śāntā* [mudrā], one should cast the left thumb downward;
then, one should encircle the right thumb with the palm of the left hand.
One should encircle the right fist with the fingers of the left hand;
this is known as the Liṅga-mudrā, which always bears the form of Śiva. || 17 ||
One should wrap the tip of the left index finger with the right hand;
having done so, one should place the thumb at the heart. 18.
Then, one should encircle the left thumb with the three fingers of the left hand;
this is declared to be the Dhvaja-mudrā, which should be employed in the ritual of sacrifice.
Having formed the añjali with both hands, one should place the two thumbs at the base of the little fingers; this is known as the āvāhanī mudrā. || 20 ||
One should join all the fingers and thumbs together, with each interlocking the next, placing the backs of the hands against each other and leaving a hollow space between the palms.
In the rite of worship, one should employ the Gāyatrī with the Gāyatrī;
for the eyes, the Netra mantra with the Netra; and for pacification, it should be performed with the face turned downwards.
Having clenched both fists together, one should quickly extend the hands;
this is known as the weapon-mudrā (astramudrā), which inspires fear in all. || 23 ||
Thus ends the ninth chapter, on the characteristics of mudrās, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṅgraha.
